gap: No result ChatGPT got states that DDPAI's N5 Dual gets radar parking only through a separate add-on module bundled with an OBD/hardwire kit (US store variant 'N5 Dual 2026 + Radar Accessory (Radar+ OBD & hardwire Kit)'), against Thinkware's radar built into the U3000/U3000 Pro front and rear units.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Thinkware help page 'RADAR Parking Mode', thinkwarestore.com/parking-mode, thinkware.com/global/product/u3000-pro and Digital Camera World's U3000 Pro review. Between them they already state the core mechanism: the camera sleeps in a low-power state and the radar wakes it to save a 20 s clip (7 s before and 13 s after an impact). They also give the 1–5 m range measured from the rear camera, the under-20 km/h target speed, interference from other 24 GHz devices and metal tint films, that Connected/LTE features are unavailable in radar mode, and that hardwiring or OBD power is required. None covers a non-Thinkware radar system. The only new part I can source is how DDPAI packages its radar (an add-on module with an OBD/hardwire kit) and DDPAI's claimed saving over time-lapse. I could not open DDPAI's own radar specs, so the finding is only partly new.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick: the Thinkware U3000 Pro stays best overall, with built-in front and rear radar and the maker's own description of radar wake with pre-event seconds. DDPAI's N5 Dual 2026 + Radar Accessory can honestly take the budget-radar segment ($269 store price on 2026-11-21 against Thinkware's $549.99 shown by ChatGPT), because the OBD/hardwire kit that radar parking needs is in the bundle. Two limits apply. DDPAI's range, standby draw and pre-buffer could not be read from DDPAI's own pages, so the page cannot claim parity on pre-event capture. And per Thinkware's own help page, a shopper who wants LTE alerts while parked loses them in Thinkware's radar mode.
candidates: Thinkware U1000 Plus with optional radar module

findings.label: How radar parking wakes and records
findings.value: Wakes from a low-power state and saves a 20-second clip: 7 s before and 13 s after an impact (10 s / 10 s for a slow approach)
findings.source_title: RADAR Parking Mode – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: Maker's help page; compatible models listed as U3000 PRO and U3000. ChatGPT cited this page.

findings.label: Radar detection range and target
findings.value: 1–5 m in five steps (default Mid, 3 m), measured from the rear camera; designed for movement slower than 20 km/h (12 mph)
findings.source_title: RADAR Parking Mode – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: Vehicles with long rears may need High or Highest. Passers-by outside the set range are not recorded.

findings.label: Radar mode limits
findings.value: THINKWARE Connected features unavailable in RADAR Parking Mode; other 24 GHz devices and metal-containing tint films can interfere; range may fail if the rear camera is not on the rear window
findings.source_title: RADAR Parking Mode – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: This contradicts ChatGPT offering 'remote alerts and live viewing' as a radar-parking priority: Connected (LTE) alerts do not run in radar mode.

findings.label: Power needed for parking mode
findings.value: Hardwiring cable or OBD II power cable required
findings.source_title: Parking Mode - THINKWARE US | Official Site
findings.note: Same page: 'U3000: Built-in Radar Module. U1000 Plus and Q1000: Optional Radar Module.' Durations on the page come from a graphic based on the separately sold 7,500 mAh iVolt Xtra battery and 'ideal conditions'; no watt figure is given in text.

findings.label: Channels, sensors and power
findings.value: 2-channel (front + rear). Front 3840×2160 at 30 fps or 2560×1440 at 60 fps, Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678. Rear 2560×1440 at 30 fps, Sony STARVIS 2 IMX675. Supercapacitor; DC 12/24 V; microSD up to 512 GB; -10 to 60 °C
findings.note: Maker claims '10% lower power consumption than the U3000', with no absolute figure. Dual radar: front and rear.

findings.label: Radar false triggers in a named review
findings.value: Default sensitivity woke the camera for rainfall, recording 'a few dozen clips of rainfall in a single night'; one notch lower fixed it
findings.source_title: Thinkware U3000 Pro review – Digital Camera World
findings.note: Same review gives $499 US for the camera and about $580 with rear camera and OBD-II cable. These prices are from the review, not a store read today. ChatGPT cited this page.

findings.label: How DDPAI sells radar for the N5 Dual
findings.value: Separate radar module sold as the variant 'N5 Dual 2026 + Radar Accessory (Radar+ OBD & hardwire Kit)', $269.00 (list $279.00)
findings.source_title: N5 Dual 2026 4K Dash Cam – DDPAI store
findings.note: Variant name and price come from the partner-store read in the brief (2026-11-21, variant id 47948271911199). I could not reopen the page because it returned HTTP 429 on each try. The base N5 Dual 2026 is $189.00 with no radar.

findings.label: DDPAI's power claim for radar parking (as reported)
findings.value: 87% lower power consumption than time-lapse recording, linked to 'up to 15 day recordings'; parking needs a separate hardwire kit
findings.source_title: DDPAI N5 DUAL 4K - Setting the Pace - Digital Reviews Network (Lis Petersen)
findings.note: Review dated 2025-07-23, so it may describe the pre-2026 N5 Dual. It gives the rear camera as 1080p, 125°. The 87% figure is DDPAI's claim relayed by the reviewer, not a measurement.

findings.label: Radar behaviour in a hands-on review
findings.value: High sensitivity 'captured video snaps of small bumps in the road or people walking by'; low-voltage cutoff is 'a software setting'
findings.source_title: DDPAI N5 Pro Review and Evaluation - 4K+2K, Radar, LTE – DashCamTalk
findings.note: Review by DashCamTalk member lufa6977, posted from 2026-09-13. The N5 Pro is not in our partner list read on 2026-11-21.
